Mitochondrial myopathy with defining progressive external ophthalmoplegia and ptosis; weakness and gait disturbance reflect muscle disease.
GRIN2B-related developmental encephalopathy with infantile spasms, severe developmental delay and absent speech.
B-lymphoblastic leukemia involving blood and bone marrow; B-cell lineage alone does not establish an immune mechanism.
Bacteroides bacterial infection; anatomical sites vary, and no particular organ is established across this umbrella.
Mitochondrial defect with severe cardiomyopathy and skeletal myopathy; pulmonary hypoplasia in 2/2 patients; neurologic findings omitted at the four-axis cap.
Renal phosphate wasting causes hypophosphatemia; nephrolithiasis and osteoporosis define this inherited syndrome.
Pulmonary arterial vascular disease with right ventricular failure in 3/5; both fall within cardiovascular, without established lung parenchymal damage.
Immune-mediated destruction of transplanted tissue; the graft organ is unspecified.
Defined by blood vessel occlusion; downstream organ damage depends on the site and is not universal across the umbrella.
Hamartomatous polyp arising in the colon or rectum.
Carcinoma originates in the endocervix, a reproductive organ outside the thirteen axes.
PRICKLE1-related progressive myoclonic epilepsy with ataxia and possible sensory neuropathy; manifestations remain within the neurologic axis.
Benign melanocytic neoplasm predominantly arising in skin; ocular and neurologic subtypes do not characterize most patients.
Lysosomal storage with hepatic dysfunction and splenic disease; impaired DLCO in 5/8 and frequent interstitial disease; bone loss omitted at cap; neuropathy <30%.
SYT1 neurodevelopmental syndrome with defining oculomotor abnormalities, frequent strabismus and impaired visual behavior; reflux is a separate disorder.
Congenital cystic malformation of pulmonary airways and lung tissue.
Painful axonal peripheral neuropathy with sensory loss and hyporeflexia; the NAGLU association alone does not establish a metabolic disorder.
Inherited retinal splitting and macular degeneration cause progressive visual impairment; complications remain within the ocular axis.
Squamous carcinoma originates in the lip or oral cavity, including buccal mucosa, tongue and gums.
Inherited focal epilepsy producing sleep-related hypermotor seizures; movement manifestations are neurologic.
Inherited cardiac conduction disorder with sinus node dysfunction, bradycardia and other rhythm abnormalities.
Congenital anterior segment dysgenesis involving the iris, pupil and anterior chamber; this concept is the ocular anomaly.
Defined by cardiomyopathy, neuropathy with distal sensory loss, and skeletal myopathy with nemaline bodies; respiratory insufficiency does not establish direct lung damage.
IKAROS-related combined immunodeficiency with low immunoglobulins; no specific additional organ damage is established.
